1.
The petitioner has filed the present petition contending that he is the owner of the land bearing khasra no. 489 and khasra no. 57/1 and his name is also recorded in the revenue records.

The Land Acquisition Officer cum Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue) has initiated proceedings for acquisition of land under the National Highway Act 1956 thereafter the award was passed on 08.03.2017 wherein the compensation has been determined but the compensation has not been disbursed to the petitioner as the respondent No. 4 has raised an objection.

Hence, this petition for following relief:-
10.1- The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to set aside the impugned order dated 28.03.2017 Annexure P/1 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer Revenue Dhamtari (CG) in case No. 11A82/2015-16.

Tikaram Gajendra vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70242702/

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the Land Acquisition Officer to disburse the amount of compensation awarded in favour of the petitioner.

10.3- The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondent Land Acquisition Officer to award interest on the amount awarded under compensation @ 18% per annum from the date of passing of the award till its disbursement to the petitioner.
10.4- The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to grant any other ancillary relief, as it may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
1-.5- Cost of the petition.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner got the property after partition and brother of the petitioner had also got the separate property in partition in the year 1988 still he is making his objection.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that since his name has been recorded in the revenue record, therefore, he is legally entitled to get compensation despite this respondent No.3 has not released the compensation.

Counsel for the petitioner would further submit that the Land Acquisition Officer has wrongly decided the issue by recording its finding that there is question of title which can be decided by the competent Civil Court, this finding is contrary to the law, since the award has been passed, therefore, compensation should have been paid to him.

3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposing the submission would submit that as per Section 3(H) of the National Highways Act, 1956, the petitioner has remedy of making claim before the competent civil Court having original jurisdiction to decide the issue, as such the writ petition is not maintainable.
4. I have head learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5. From the record, it is quite vivid that the land was acquired for construction of National Highway No. 30/43 Raipur Dhamtari.
The land acquisition proceedings for National Highway is governed by the National Highways Act, 1956 which provides complete mechanism for resolving the issue raised under the Act.
Section 3(H) of the Act provides manner and procedure of depositing and payment of amount of compensation.

For better understanding the facts involved in the case it is expedient for this Court to extract Section 3(H) which reads as under:-
Section 3H. Deposit and payment of amount.--
(1) The amount determined under section 3G shall be deposited by the Central Government in such manner as may be laid down by rules made in this behalf by that Government, with the competent authority before taking possession of the land.

(2)
As soon as may be after the amount has been deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall on behalf of the Central Government pay the amount to the person or persons entitled thereto.

sentences.text: (3) Where several persons claim to be interested in the amount deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority shall determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.

(4) If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

(5) Where the amount determined under section 3G by the arbitrator is in excess of the amount determined by the competent authority, the arbitrator may award interest at nine per cent, per annum on such excess amount from the date of taking possession under section 3D till the date of the actual deposit thereof.
(6) Where the amount determined by the arbitrator is in excess of the amount determined by the competent authority, the excess amount together with interest, if any, awarded under sub-section.

(7) shall be deposited by the Central Government in such manner as may be laid down by rules made in this behalf by that Government, with the competent authority and the provisions of sub- sections (2) to (4) shall apply to such deposit.

6. From perusal of Section 3(H)(4) of the Act, It is quite vivid that if there is dispute with regard to apportionment amount of compensation or any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable the competent authority shall refer to the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.
Since there is dispute about apportionment of the compensation, therefore, the matter has to be referred to the principal civil court for adjudication.

Section 3(H) of the Act, 1956 has come up for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 5107 of 2022 in the case of Vinod Kumar and Ors. vs. District Magistrate Mau & Ors on 07.07.2023 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in paragraph 34 and 35 as under:-
34.

entities.text: Vinod Kumar and Ors. vs. District Magistrate Mau & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Our final conclusion is as under: If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amo2019unt or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, then, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

The competent authority possesses certain powers of the Civil Court, but in the event of a dispute of the a2019bove nature, the summary power, vesting in the competent authority of rendering an opinion in terms of subsection (3) of Section 3H, will not serve the purpose.
The dispute being of the nature triable by the Civil Court that the law steps in to provide for that to be referred to the decision of the Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction.
The dispute regarding apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, would then have to be decided by that Court.
35. In such circumstance referred to above, the order passed by the District Magistrate, Mau dated 16.01.2020 is hereby quashed and set aside.
The writ application No. 7310 of 2020 stands allowed.

3 parties as regards apportionment of the amount of compensation, the Special Land Acquisition Officer shall now refer the dispute to the Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction in accordance with sub clause (4) of Section 3H of the Act 1956.

sentences.text:
7. Considering the submission made by counsel for the parties, also considering the Section 3H of the Act, 1956 and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Vinod Kumar (supra), since there is dispute regarding apportionment of the amount of compensation Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue) has rightly observed that the right and the title of the property which can be adjudicated by the competent Civil Court, therefore, the claim of compensation withheld by him cannot said to be illegal or contrary to the provisions of law, but the learned Sub Divisional Officer/
Land Acquisition Officer committed illegality in not referring the matter to principal Civil Court for adjudication in accordance with the provisions of Act, 1956, therefore,
the writ petition is partly allowed.

The Sub Divisional 1Officer (Revenue)/ Land Acquisition Officer Dhamtari is directed to refer to 41the dispute to the principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction in accordance with sub clause 4 of Section 3H of the Act,
1956 within two months from the date of receipt of the copy of the order.

It is also directed that on reference being made by the Land Acquisition Officer, concerning principal Civil Court Dhamtari will make an endeavor to complete the proceeding within outer limit of one year from the date of reference keeping in view the fact that the award was passed on 08.03.2017 and the petitioner has not received compensation for more than 6 years.
